title: Natural Deduction in First-Order Logic
subtopics: Substitution σ: X → T and its domain
Extension σ̂: T → T of a substitution to terms
Application of substitution to formulae σ̂(φ)
Soundness and completeness of FOL natural deduction

definitions.definition: A function σ: X → T such that σ(x) ≠ x for only finitely many variables x.
dom(σ) = {x ∈ X | σ(x) ≠ x}, the finite set of variables that are actually replaced.
σ̂: T → T defined inductively: σ̂(x) = σ(x), σ̂(c) = c, σ̂(f(t₁,…,tₙ)) = f(σ̂(t₁),…,σ̂(tₙ)).
σ is safe for variable x in formula φ if no free occurrence of x in φ becomes bound after applying σ.
From ∀x.φ, derive φ[x ↦ t] for any term t, provided the substitution is safe.
From φ (where x does not appear free in any assumption), derive ∀x.φ.

algorithms: Application of substitution σ to a formula φ
formulas: φ[x ↦ t] denotes applying substitution {x ↦ t} to φ
∀I: if x ∉ free(Γ), then Γ ⊢ φ implies Γ ⊢ ∀x.φ
∃E: from ∃x.φ and φ ⊢ ψ (x ∉ free(ψ)), derive ψ
learning_objectives: Define substitutions and compute their application to terms and formulae.
Apply the ∀I, ∀E, ∃I, ∃E rules of natural deduction for FOL.
Construct natural deduction proofs for FOL sequents.
